memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'All who are skilled among you are to come and make everything the Lord has commanded: the tabernacle with its tent and its covering, clasps, frames, crossbars, posts and bases; the ark with its poles and the atonement cover and the curtain that shields it; the table with its poles and all its articles and the bread of the Presence.'" - Exod 35:10-13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God asked for materials. Now He asks for ability.

"All who are skilled among you are to come." Some had nothing valuable to donate but knew how to work wood, weave cloth, or set stone. Their offering was their competence, and God wanted it just as much as He wanted gold.

This dignifies ordinary work in a way we often miss. The carpenter who shaped the frames was doing sacred work. So was the weaver. Their trade — learned in Egypt, probably under slavery — became worship.

Your skills are not spiritually neutral. The ability to teach, to cook, to fix machinery, to manage accounts, to comfort a frightened child, to write clearly — these are given by God and can be given back to Him. Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord (Col 3:23).

Notice the detail in the list too. Poles, clasps, bases, crossbars. God cares about the parts nobody photographs. Excellence in hidden things matters to Him.

And see what stands at the centre: the ark with its atonement cover. Everything else surrounded the place where mercy met a broken covenant — which is where all our work finally finds its meaning too.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What skills has God given you that you have never thought of as offerings?
2. Do you bring the same care to unseen work as to visible work?
3. How could your ordinary occupation become worship this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You gave me whatever ability I have. I offer my hands and my work back to You today. Amen.
